Subject: Ascend renewal: 12-month term swap + capacity uplift — initial package

Hi Susan / Ravi,

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. Per our plan, attached is a clean order form (redline_orderform_v3.pdf) and our proposed MSA redline (proposed_msa_redline.pdf) that implements the following at a high level: 
- Move to a 12-month term (from current 24-month cadence) effective at next renewal date
- Capacity uplift: +40% reserved capacity across the inference pool (Exhibit B) for the first 6 months, then auto-step to +20% thereafter
- Pricing: blended rate to reflect the committed uplift — details in the order form

We expect a short legal review on the MSA items. Two specific items I flagged for Ascend in the order form: 1) data residency carve (Section 7) and 2) termination/early-exit language tied to usage thresholds (Section 12).

Can you confirm you received the attachments and whether Ascend has any immediate redlines? If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute legal touchpoint this week — Jordan, Kimberly (Sales Ops) and Markus (Legal) can join from our side.

Target timeline: get to an agreed tracked-changes set by EOD 2029-10-04 so we can route to DocuSign the following week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Thanks for sending this over. We reviewed the drafts with product and legal and have attached our marked MSA (ascend_marked_msa.pdf). High level: we like the shorter 12-month term, but legal has three items they want addressed before we can sign:

1) Data residency: we need a firm commitment that customer data processed for specific EU tenants will remain in EU regions (Section 7).
2) Termination for convenience: shorten to 45 days notice (we proposed 30, Redwood currently proposes 60).
3) Indemnity carve: minor rewording around third-party claims for model outputs.

I've annotated the MSA with line comments; Ravi will follow up on the technical side re: routing to EU endpoints. Can we get DG (your legal) to propose counter language for 1 and 3?

Also — we attached a PDF of our in-line comments. Let us know availability for a legal sync Thurs or Fri.

Best,
Susan Park
Head of Platform, Ascend AI
susan@ascend.ai

Kimberly / Markus / Monica — forwarding Ascend's marked MSA and the three asks below.

Priority items for legal to weigh in on:
- Data residency (Ascend requests EU-only processing for specific tenant IDs) — our platform supports region pinning but the MSA needs explicit contractual language.
- Termination for convenience period — Ascend asks 45 days (they proposed 30); they are willing to compromise if we accept a 45-day window.
- Indemnity carve for model outputs — their redline tightens scope; we likely want to preserve reasonable limitations.

Please advise suggested tracked-change language for each item and whether we can accept the 45-day termination compromise. Customer asked for a legal touchpoint on 2029-10-04 (Thu) between 10:00-11:00 PT — can Markus or someone from legal join?

Thanks —
Jordan

Subject: RE: Fwd: Ascend marked MSA — legal suggested language

Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks for the flag. Quick read and position:

1) Data residency (Section 7) — acceptable to commit to processing Ascend tenant data in EU regions for EU-designated tenant IDs. Suggested clause: "Redwood will, upon Customer's reasonable request and where technically feasible, process Customer Data originating from EU-designated tenant IDs in EU-based regions. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain data residency and will document any exception windows in writing." This preserves operational limitations while giving Ascend a contractual promise.

2) Termination for convenience — we can accept a 45-day notice window for the 12-month renewal term only (not for existing longer legacy deals). That is a reasonable commercial compromise; suggested tracked language included in attached redline_response.pdf.

3) Indemnity for model outputs — pushback: we should not create broad open indemnities for model outputs. Proposed middle-ground: limit obligation to material breach of warranty or willful misconduct and carve out anonymized third-party data. Language in redline_response.pdf.

Next steps: Jordan, please share redline_response.pdf with Susan and propose the legal-only sync on Thu 10/04 10:30 PT. If Ascend signs off on the three items above, we can get the order form into DocuSign next week.

-Markus
General Counsel (acting), Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: redline_response.pdf

Subject: Counterproposal and next steps — Ascend renewal (DocuSign link included)

Susan / Ravi —

Appreciate you taking the time to review. Attached is our counterproposal (redline_response.pdf) with tracked changes that reflect the legal compromises Markus outlined below. Short summary of what we propose: 

1) Data residency: Redwood will commit to processing EU-designated tenant data in EU regions and will include an exceptions addendum with documented timelines for unavoidable migrations or emergency failovers.
2) Termination: Redwood accepts a 45-day termination-for-convenience notice for the upcoming 12-month term only.
3) Indemnity: Redwood will limit indemnity for model outputs to breaches of express warranties and will exclude downstream anonymized data and general model behavior.

Please review the attached tracked changes. If acceptable, the order form is staged in DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/eq/Sign?cm=docu-ascend-orderform-102. Target signature date: 2029-10-16 to honor renewal timing and preserve pricing.

If Ascend wants to hold a brief legal call to confirm specific wording, Markus is available next Tue 10/15 09:00-09:30 PT. Otherwise, please confirm by reply and sign the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
